text:
Alex: Thinking about the canary policy UX — should we land on probabilistic sampling + short smoothing window, or deterministic holdback (sticky 10%) with explicit abort?
Maria: leaning probabilistic for smaller tenants. easier to average out noise. :thinking_face:
Cheng: probabilistic helps when traffic is bursty, but it makes debugging tail-latency regressions harder bc the sample isn't stable per-tenant.
Natalie: ops perspective: deterministic holdback + sticky routing means a single tenant always goes to the new variant until we flip. Easier for customer debug and rollbacks.
Alex: right. tradeoffs: stability vs faster signal. Also cost gating — if we do probabilistic sampling we need to account for token-cost spikes from noisy users.
Maria: what about hybrid? deterministic holdback for 5% of tenants (sticky), and an additional 5% probabilistic across all tenants to get faster aggregate metrics.
Cheng: hybrid seems promising. We can surface both signals in console: cohort-stable (deterministic) + sample-based (probabilistic). Need clear labels.
Natalie: autoscaling+auto-pause rule question: if sample-based latency crosses 95th percentile SLO but deterministic cohort is fine, should we pause? Feels noisy to pause on sample alone.
Alex: propose rule: auto-pause requires at least two independent signals: (a) cohort-stable breach OR (b) sample-based breach sustained for >3m AND cost delta > X%.
Maria: +1. We should quantify X. Ops wants to avoid pauses for small cost blips. Maybe X = 15% token cost increase or absolute +$0.20/min for top-of-stack?
Cheng: instead of dollar threshold, we should use relative per-tenant cost delta with a floor. e.g. delta >= 15% AND delta >= $0.10/min. That avoids tiny tenants causing global pauses.
Natalie: also add a debounce window and exponential backoff on auto-pause to avoid flip-flopping. Example: 3m sustained -> pause, then cool-down 10m, then allow one manual resume or auto-resume only after 30m with stable metrics.
Alex: UX: console controls for rollout should show: traffic split (sticky vs sampled), smoothing window, auto-pause sensitivity (cost % and tail-slo percentile), and backoff settings. slider + advanced YAML view.
Maria: telemetry needs: per-cohort p50/p95/p99 latency, token-rate, token-cost-rate, request-error-rate, and cardinality keys (tenant, route, model). Also show number of requests in deterministic cohort vs sampled pool.
Cheng: we must be careful with percentile calculations for sampled pool. If we sample 5% globally, p99 will be noisy unless we increase sampling for tail analysis. Add an on-demand sampling boost for problematic routes.
Natalie: ops-bot just fired a test alert for the synthetic canary today, FYI.
ops-bot: Automated alert: synthetic-canary latency p95 crossed threshold on route /v1/generate at 2024-11-28T14:07Z — metric source: sampled cohort.
Alex: perfect example — sampled cohort alerted but deterministic tenants stable. We shouldn't auto-pause yet. Maria can you add the "require two signals" rule to the rollout guard PR?
Maria: on it. I'll draft the YAML for the rollout guard. Rough version: ```guard:
  require_signals: 2
  signals:
    - cohort_stable: p95 > 800ms
    - sampled_sustained: p95 > 900ms for >180s
  cost_condition:
    relative_increase_pct: 15
    absolute_increase_usd_per_min: 0.10
  backoff:
    initial_cooldown_min: 10
    auto_resume_after_min: 30
```
Cheng: add an opt-in debugging flag to mark certain tenants for high-fidelity sampling (100% for 10m) to repro tail issues. Must be gated by RBAC.
Natalie: +1. Also add an audit event when auto-pause triggers with the signals that caused it. Helps SRE postmortems.
Alex: ok action items: Maria draft PR with YAML + console mocks, Cheng add per-tenant high-fidelity sampling flag and ensure metric continuity, Natalie define alert thresholds for dual-signal pause, I'll wire the UI labels and copy.
Maria: I'll ping infra for an additional metrics retention tweak for sampled cohorts.
Cheng: one more thing: document in internal runbook that sampled-signal-only pauses are 'advisory' and require manual confirmation unless cost delta condition met.
Natalie: noted.
Alex: thanks team. Short follow-up in this thread when PR is up. :raised_hands:
